correctness.rationale: The centralizer equation is exactly [A,B]=0 and Av=Bu. The map Phi from the matrix centralizer into V/im(A) has rank the number of zero-primary Jordan blocks no longer than the largest occupied block: a module homomorphism cannot map an L-block top onto a longer-block top, and explicit homomorphisms to every shorter-block top show surjectivity. This establishes the general rank formula for all fields. Finite-field vector fibers are counted by independent top coordinates; summing over rational-canonical classes gives the rank polynomial. All seventeen n=3 characteristic-polynomial/Jordan strata have been symbolically enumerated and checked. Independent full direct ad-matrix enumeration over F2 in dimension three recovered 4096 elements and 86080 commuting ordered pairs.

originality.rationale: Searches of matrix-commuting class theory, enhanced nilpotent cone orbit classification, classical finite Lie-algebra commuting pair formulas, and affine GROUP conjugacy formulas reveal the substantial relevant mechanisms but no explicit all-matrix-part affine LIE adjoint-rank weights or the seven-polynomial dimension-three distribution. The strongest close case, Fulman–Guralnick 2021 §3.1, counts invertible affine GROUP conjugacy classes and establishes highest-block orbit representatives; it neither covers singular matrix parts nor gives dimensions of Lie centralizers, so its displayed theorems do not imply the explicit n=3 rank-spectrum formula without a new passage and enumeration. Bibliographic completeness cannot be guaranteed.
residual_risks: The literature contains closely related enhanced/mirabolic orbit theory, and an unlocated presentation might yield the same Lie-rank distribution.
No claim of exhaustive bibliographic priority or independent external review; general dimension enumeration remains an exact finite sum, not a simplified product.

value.rationale: This is a natural global distribution for adjoint operators and commuting pairs in the non-reductive affine-transformation Lie algebra over every finite field. It distinguishes contributions from the singular zero-primary structure invisible in matrix centralizers alone and gives a closed factored seven-fiber count for the first nontrivial dimension n=3, including a non-obvious absence of ranks 1,2,4,10,11,12. The result is mathematically stronger than isolated experiments or a normalization check and is useful as a reference case for nonreductive commuting varieties and their finite-point counts.
